rules.description: Input, output, representation, and deterministic tie-breaking agree across problem text, code, and tests.
The implementation is correct for normal, empty, boundary, and declared failure cases.
Reasoning prompts target a concrete invariant or mechanism rather than generic words such as invariant or algorithm.
Declared time and space bounds match the implementation and assumptions.
Boundaries distinguish unsupported inputs, detected invalid cases, and actual runtime failures.
Executable tests cover the contract and distinguish implementation variants.
One AlgorithmUnit owns all applicable practice modes; modes are not duplicated as separate templates.
Concept keys are specific enough for deterministic scoring and aliases are reviewed expressions.
Transfer content states what transfers, what differs, and where the pattern stops applying.
Each implementation has a stable key and explicit strategy, complexity, assumptions, and relevant practice references.
Generated source and test references stay inside the draft root.
Generated code is executed only in a bounded validation subprocess; template content cannot supply commands.
Publishable factual content has authoritative sources and compatible licensing.
Model output cannot self-assign reviewed, validated, or accepted state.
